sentences.en: Democrats and Republicans doing what almost no one thought they could, reaching a deal on guns.
sentences.zh: 民主党人和共和党人正在做几乎没人认为他们能做到的事：就枪支问题达成协议。

sentences.en: The Senate has reached a bipartisan deal on gun safety that could put Congress on a path to the most significant federal response to gun violence in decades.
sentences.zh: 参议院已就枪支安全达成了一项两党协议，这可能使国会走上几十年来应对枪支暴力最重大的联邦行动之路。

sentences.en: There's going to be incentives for states to implement red flag laws that deny guns to people deemed a risk to themselves or others.
sentences.zh: 协议将为各州实施“红旗法”提供激励措施，拒绝向被认为对自己或他人构成风险的人提供枪支。

sentences.en: There's also enhanced background checks for 18 to 21 year olds in this country.
sentences.zh: 此外，该国还将加强对18至21岁人群的背景调查。

sentences.en: There's funding for mental health, school safety funding, a provision addressing the, quote, boyfriend loophole on domestic violence, and another provision.
sentences.zh: 协议还包括心理健康资金、学校安全资金，以及一项旨在解决家庭暴力中所谓“男友漏洞”的条款，还有其他规定。

sentences.en: Today, I spoke with a senator who's at the center of those negotiations, Chris Murphy
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了处于这些谈判核心的参议员——来自康涅狄格州的克里斯·墨菲，

sentences.en: of Connecticut, about how the deal was reached, how meaningful it actually is, and what it reveals about a new strategy for gun control.
sentences.zh: 谈到了该协议是如何达成的，它的实际意义，以及它揭示了枪支管制的新策略。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月14日，星期二。

sentences.en: Senator Murphy, hi.
sentences.zh: 墨菲参议员，你好。

sentences.en: I think you're muted.
sentences.zh: 我想你静音了。

sentences.en: There we go.
sentences.zh: 好了，可以了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thank you for taking the time with us.
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: So I want to get to the deal that you and your Republican colleagues made over the past few weeks.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你和你的共和党同事在过去几周达成的协议。

sentences.en: But first of all, I wanted to understand how this deal was reached and your role in it.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我想了解这个协议是如何达成的，以及你在其中扮演的角色。

sentences.en: You represent the state of Connecticut, which is where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你代表的是康涅狄格州，也就是美国

sentences.en: first experienced a mass shooting at an elementary school.
sentences.zh: 首次发生小学大规模枪击案的地方。

sentences.en: So I wanted to go back just a couple of weeks to
sentences.zh: 所以我想回到几周前，

sentences.en: May 24th.
That was, of course, the day of the mass shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde,
sentences.zh: 那当然就是德克萨斯州尤瓦尔迪市罗布小学发生大规模枪击案的那一天。

sentences.en: Texas.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: And you ended up on the Senate floor a few minutes after it happened.
sentences.zh: 事件发生几分钟后，你就出现在了参议院议事厅。

sentences.en: And I wanted to talk about that speech.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈那次演讲。

sentences.en: So can you describe what was going through your head?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下当时你的脑海里在想什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, I was actually presiding over the Senate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时实际上正在主持参议院会议。

sentences.en: I was sitting in the vice president's chair on the dais when I learned that this was a shooting of scope similar to Sandy Hook.
sentences.zh: 我坐在主席台副总统的椅子上，当时我得知这是一起规模类似于桑迪胡克小学的枪击案。

sentences.en: And I just first and foremost think about the parents in Sandy Hook when a shooting like this happens.
sentences.zh: 每当发生这样的枪击案，我首先想到的就是桑迪胡克的家长们。

sentences.en: I mean, especially
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特别是

sentences.en: Uvalde, which was so tragically reminiscent of Sandy Hook.
sentences.zh: 尤瓦尔迪，它悲剧性地让人想起了桑迪胡克。

sentences.en: You have to realize that, you know,
sentences.zh: 你必须意识到，你知道，

sentences.en: Sandy Hook never recovered and will never recover.
sentences.zh: 桑迪胡克从未恢复，也永远无法恢复。

sentences.en: And those parents are forced to relive that nightmare, right?
sentences.zh: 那些家长被迫重温那场噩梦，对吧？

sentences.en: When something like Uvalde happens, they look at those images of the parents waiting outside
sentences.zh: 当尤瓦尔迪这样的事情发生时，他们看着那些家长在学校外等待的画面，

sentences.en: the school and they remember being in the firehouse as it emptied out and there was only 20 sets of parents left.
sentences.zh: 他们会想起自己当时在消防站等待，直到最后只剩下20对父母的情景。

sentences.en: I was there.
sentences.zh: 我就在那里。

sentences.en: I saw all of that.
sentences.zh: 我目睹了这一切。

sentences.en: Obviously, I was just an interloper to their grief, but all of that comes flooding back.
sentences.zh: 显然，对于他们的悲伤来说，我只是个局外人，但所有的一切都涌上心头。

sentences.en: And I was both at the same time furious and absolutely heartbroken.
sentences.zh: 当时我既愤怒又无比心碎。

sentences.en: Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 议长先生。

sentences.en: Senator from Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 来自康涅狄格州的参议员。

sentences.en: I came down from the dais and I went straight to my desk.
sentences.zh: 我从主席台上走下来，径直走向我的座位。

sentences.en: Just days after a shooter walked into a grocery store to gun down African
sentences.zh: 就在一名枪手走进杂货店枪杀非裔美国顾客几天后，我们又面临了另一场“桑迪胡克”。

sentences.en: American patrons, we have another Sandy Hook on our hands.
sentences.zh: 我没有写下任何东西。

sentences.en: I hadn't written anything out.
sentences.zh: 我没有做任何准备。

sentences.en: I hadn't prepared anything.
sentences.zh: 我只是说出了我脑海里的想法。

sentences.en: I just said what was in my head.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子每次踏进教室都生活在恐惧中，因为他们认为下一个可能就是自己。

sentences.en: Our kids are living in fear every single time they set foot in the classroom because I think they're going to be next.
sentences.zh: 我们到底在做什么？

sentences.en: What are we doing?
sentences.zh: 听着，这对我们所有人来说都是个人的事，但我有一个上四年级的孩子。

sentences.en: And listen, this is personal for all of us, but I have a fourth grader.
sentences.zh: 在桑迪胡克枪击案发生时，我的儿子离上幼儿园和一年级还有一两年。

sentences.en: And at the time of the Sandy
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当然，当我处理这些悲剧并想到桑迪胡克时，

sentences.en: Hook shooting, I had a son who was just a year or two away from going into kindergarten and first grade.
sentences.zh: 我会想到我自己的孩子，想到我四年级的儿子在尤瓦尔迪事件发生后的第二天，

sentences.en: And so, you know, of course, when I process these tragedies and when I think about Sandy Hook,
sentences.zh: 与同学们讨论他们会怎么做、躲在哪里，以及是否要像尤瓦尔迪那个小女孩一样在脸上涂满血迹。

sentences.en: I think about my own kids and I think about the conversations that my fourth grader was going to have
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，作为参议院中为数不多的有年幼孩子的家长之一，

sentences.en: the day after Uvalde with his classmates about what they would do and where they would hide and whether they would smear blood on their face like the little girl did in Uvalde.
sentences.zh: 我感受得更深，也以不同的方式思考着桑迪胡克的故事。

sentences.en: So for me, it was one of the few parents of young kids in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 在桑迪胡克小学，那些孩子回到教室后，他们不得不采取一种做法，即设定一个安全词，

sentences.en: I also feel this more deeply and sort of think about those stories from Sandy Hook in a different way.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在白天开始做噩梦，重温试图逃离学校时跨过同学尸体的场景，他们就会说出这个词。

sentences.en: In Sandy Hook Elementary School, after those kids came back into those classrooms, they had to adopt a practice in which there would be a safe word that
sentences.zh: 在一个教室里，那个词是“猴子”。

sentences.en: the kids would say if they started to get nightmares during the day, reliving, stepping over their classmates' bodies as they tried to flee the school.
sentences.zh: 整整一天，孩子们会一遍又一遍地站起来大喊“猴子”。

sentences.en: In one classroom, that word was monkey.
sentences.zh: 老师或辅助人员必须走到那个孩子身边，把他们带出教室，和他们谈谈他们所看到的一切，帮助他们解决心理问题。

sentences.en: And over and over and over through the day, kids would stand up and yell monkey.
sentences.zh: 桑迪胡克永远、永远不会再一样了。

sentences.en: And a teacher or a paraprofessional would have to go over to that kid, take them out of the classroom, talk to them about what they had seen, work them through their issues.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州的这个社区也永远、永远不会再一样了。

sentences.en: Sandy Hook will never, ever be the same.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: This community in Texas will never, ever be the same.
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会在这里？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个挑战我同事的时刻。

sentences.en: Why are we here?
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个确保参议院承担责任的时刻。

sentences.en: I knew this was a moment to challenge my colleagues.
sentences.zh: 你花这么多时间竞选美国参议员是为了什么？

sentences.en: I knew this was a moment to make sure that there was accountability in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 你为什么要经历这么多麻烦？

sentences.en: Why do you spend all this time running for the United States Senate?
sentences.zh: 为了得到这份工作？

sentences.en: Why do you go through all the hassle?
sentences.zh: 为了让自己处于权威地位？

sentences.en: Of getting this job?
sentences.zh: 如果你的答案是，随着屠杀的增加，随着我们的孩子为生命而奔逃，我们却什么都不做。

sentences.en: Of putting yourself in a position of authority?
sentences.zh: 我们到底在做什么？

sentences.en: If your answer is that as this slaughter increases, as our kids run for their lives, we do nothing.
sentences.zh: 你为什么在这里？

sentences.en: What are we doing?
sentences.zh: 最后，我恳求我的共和党同事们坐到谈判桌前。

sentences.en: Why are you here?
sentences.zh: 我站在这里，恳求，甚至是跪下来恳求我的同事们。

sentences.en: And I ended up making a plea to my Republican colleagues to come to the table.
sentences.zh: 找到一条前进的道路。

sentences.en: I'm here on this floor to beg, to literally get down on my hands and knees and beg my colleagues.
sentences.zh: 与我们合作，找到通过法律的方法，让这种事情发生的可能性降低。

sentences.en: Find a path forward here.
sentences.zh: 我明白我的共和党同事不会同意我支持的一切，但我们可以找到一个共同点。

sentences.en: Work with us to find a way to pass laws that make this less likely.
sentences.zh: 我放弃发言权。

sentences.en: I understand my Republican colleagues will not agree to everything that I may support, but there is a common denominator that we can find.
sentences.zh: 参议员，正如你所说，你那天在演讲结束时确实是在恳求你的同事。

sentences.en: Healed the floor.
sentences.zh: 这在我看来，就像是你承认几乎没有任何机会真正达成什么成果。

sentences.en: Senator, as you said, you ended your speech that day by literally begging your colleagues.
sentences.zh: 感觉，参议员，请不要误解，但感觉很绝望。

sentences.en: And that seemed to me like you were acknowledging that there was virtually no chance of anything really happening.
sentences.zh: 我确实感到绝望。

sentences.en: It felt, and Senator, please don't take this the wrong way, but it felt desperate.
sentences.zh: 我已经绝望了10年。

sentences.en: I do feel desperate.
sentences.zh: 我曾与多位共和党参议员参与过关于改变枪支法的讨论。

sentences.en: I felt desperate for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 但它们从来没有取得任何进展。

sentences.en: And I've been involved in talks about changing our gun laws with multiple Republican senators.
sentences.zh: 最终，你知道，我们没能找到共同点，或者时机过去了，谈判也就结束了。

sentences.en: They've just never gone anywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时确实很绝望，我在那天站在议事厅里，没有提出任何要求，对吧？

sentences.en: Eventually, you know, we weren't able to find common ground or the moment faded and the talks ended.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我只是说，坐到谈判桌前吧。

sentences.en: And so I certainly was desperate and I was on the floor that day making no demands, right?
sentences.zh: 让我们找到共同点。

sentences.en: I mean, I was just saying, come to the table.
sentences.zh: 我不会让“完美”成为“好”的敌人。

sentences.en: Let's find the common denominator.
sentences.zh: 我希望我那天表达的方式，确实创造了一个比过去人们认为的更安全的空间，让共和党人能够坐到谈判桌前。

sentences.en: I will not let the perfect be the enemy of the good.
sentences.zh: 没有先决条件，没有红线。

sentences.en: And my hope is that the way that I framed it that day did create a safer space than maybe folks have thought existed in the past for Republicans to come to the table.
sentences.zh: 让我们找出我们可以共同做的一系列事情。

sentences.en: No preconditions, no red lines.
sentences.zh: 我希望我当时所拥有的、并且至今仍然拥有的那种绝望感，是说服一些共和党人进行对话的部分原因。

sentences.en: Let's just find the set of things that we can do together.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们谈谈那个，参议员。

sentences.en: And I hope that that desperation that I did have and I still have today is part of what convinced a few Republicans to talk.
sentences.zh: 当你离开议事厅时发生了什么？

sentences.en: So let's talk about that, Senator.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我做的第一件事就是给约翰·科宁发短信。

sentences.en: What happened when you left the floor?
sentences.zh: 来自德克萨斯州的参议员。

sentences.en: Well, you know, the first thing I did was to text John Cornyn.
sentences.zh: 来自德克萨斯州的参议员。

sentences.en: Senator from Texas.
sentences.zh: 然后给德克萨斯州的另一位参议员泰德·克鲁兹发短信。

sentences.en: Senator from Texas.
sentences.zh: 只是简单地说我在挂念他们，我知道他们正在经历什么，他们的社区正在经历什么，我随时准备提供帮助。

sentences.en: And then to text the other senator from Texas, Ted Cruz.
sentences.zh: 约翰和我长期以来一直是同事和朋友。

sentences.en: And just to say simply that I was thinking of them and that I knew what they were going through and what their communities were going through and that I was there to help.
sentences.zh: 他回信说谢谢，并说他正前往尤瓦尔迪。

sentences.en: John and I have been colleagues and friends for a long time.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的24小时里，我们计划在他回到华盛顿时会面。

sentences.en: He texted me back to say thanks and that he was heading to Uvalde.
sentences.zh: 在同一时间段内，克里斯汀·希内玛向我表达了参与的兴趣。

sentences.en: And over the course of the next 24 hours, we made a plan to meet when he returned to Washington.
sentences.zh: 她与共和党人有很多非常稳固的关系。

sentences.en: During that same amount of time, Kirsten Sinema expressed an interest to me in getting involved.
sentences.zh: 我知道她确实可以成为讨论中非常有价值的补充。

sentences.en: And she has a lot of very strong relationships with Republicans.
sentences.zh: 到了周四，我们安排了一次小规模会议，参加者包括希内玛参议员、我本人、

sentences.en: I knew that she could really be a valuable addition to discussions.
sentences.zh: 来自德克萨斯州的科宁参议员和来自北卡罗来纳州的提利斯参议员。

sentences.en: And by Thursday, we had a small meeting set up between Senator Sinema, myself,
sentences.zh: 正是在那次会议上，我们开始敲定我刚才在参议院议事厅提到的那个共同点。

sentences.en: Senator Cornyn from Texas, and Senator Tillis from North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，这份清单比我预想的要长。

sentences.en: And it was in that meeting that we started to hammer out what could be that common denominator that I talked about on the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 所以我在周四离开那次会议，以及后来我们与更大规模的共和党团体进行的另一次会议后，

sentences.en: And to my surprise, the list was longer than I might have thought was available.
sentences.zh: 心想显然存在一些以前从未有过的机会。

sentences.en: And so I walked away from that meeting on Thursday and then another meeting we had done with a bigger group of
sentences.zh: 参议员，你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: Republicans, thinking to myself that there was clearly some opportunity that hadn't existed before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，共和党人愿意谈论改变枪支法。

sentences.en: And Senator, why do you think that was?
sentences.zh: 为什么是这所学校？

sentences.en: I mean, Republicans were willing to talk about changes to gun laws.
sentences.zh: 为什么这次枪击案之后他们愿意谈，而桑迪胡克之后却不愿意？

sentences.en: Why this school?
sentences.zh: 我目前还不知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: Why this shooting when they weren't after Sandy Hook?
sentences.zh: 我有一些猜测。

sentences.en: I don't know the answer to that question yet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，首先，我认为我在过去两周学到的是，所有那些失败的谈判都是这一刻的前提。

sentences.en: I have some guesses.
sentences.zh: 我们能够让共和党人更自在地进行对话，让他们稍微走出舒适区，这样当这一刻到来时，

sentences.en: You know, first of all, what I think I've learned in the last two weeks is that all of those failed negotiations were a predicate to this point.
sentences.zh: 有更多人愿意坐下来进行真正取得成果的对话。

sentences.en: We were able to get Republicans more comfortable with talking, got them to get a little bit more outside their comfort zone, so that when this moment arrived,
sentences.zh: 我认为发生的第二件事是，每个人都回家度过了阵亡将士纪念日的休会周。

sentences.en: there were more that were willing to sit down and have a talk that actually led to fruition.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，当立法进程有动力时，这是一个非常冒险的事情。

sentences.en: I think the second thing that happened was that everybody went home for the Memorial Day recess week.

sentences.en: And I think that was important to sort of keep folks at the table.

sentences.en: The second thing was to just be creative, finding that common ground to sort of cast a wide net.

sentences.en: And so we started with a lot of potential changes and we ended up with five, but that's five more than would have been possible a year ago.

sentences.en: State.
sentences.zh: 这项法案将包括一项联邦层面的枪支贩运禁令。

sentences.en: They're bought in South Carolina or Georgia, places where they don't have to go through a background check online or at a gun store.
sentences.zh: 此外，联邦层面也没有针对代购行为的法规。

sentences.en: They buy a mess load of weapons and then they bring them up to New York and sell them.
sentences.zh: 所以在康涅狄格州这样实行普遍背景调查的地方，经常发生的情况是，某个被禁止买枪的人，比如有重罪记录的人，

sentences.en: There is no effective federal statute prohibiting that scheme.
sentences.zh: 派别人去帮他们买枪。

sentences.en: This bill would include a federal prohibition on gun trafficking.
sentences.zh: 这种代购行为目前作为联邦犯罪几乎无法执行。

sentences.en: Further, there's no statute federally against straw purchasing.
sentences.zh: 我们的法案将使其成为联邦犯罪，并大幅提高处罚力度。

sentences.en: So what happens a lot in a place like Connecticut where you have universal background checks is someone who's prohibited from buying a gun, someone who's got a felony record,
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: sends somebody else in to buy the gun for them.
sentences.zh: 我们没能让共和党人同意提高购买攻击性武器的年龄限制。

sentences.en: That straw purchase is right now virtually unenforceable as a federal crime.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经实施并将实施一项针对18至20岁购买者的强化背景调查，这实际上将禁止他们立即获得枪支。

sentences.en: Our bill would make it a federal crime and would dramatically elevate the penalties.
sentences.zh: 这需要几天时间。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 那个冷静期对于像尤瓦尔迪枪手那样处于危机中的人来说很重要。

sentences.en: We weren't able to get Republicans to agree to raise the age on the purchase of assault weapons.
sentences.zh: 而那种更全面的背景调查将使我们能够，你知道，确保这个年轻人有责任拥有那种武器。

sentences.en: But we have put into place and will put into place an enhanced background check for 18 to 20 year old purchasers that will actually prohibit them from getting a gun immediately.
sentences.zh: 这会带来改变。

sentences.en: It'll take a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 但参议员，另一方面，如你所知，你的一些民主党同事，特别是在众议院，说这太软弱了，你在这个过程中给了共和党人太多的权力，

sentences.en: That cooling off period will be important for people that are in crisis like the Uvalde shooter.
sentences.zh: 你不应该同意如此狭隘的方案，因为共和党人只会说他们做了一些事情，然后就不会再回到这个问题上，这就是终点了。

sentences.en: And that more comprehensive background check will allow us to, you know, just make absolutely sure that this young person is in a responsible position to own that weapon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你显然对此有不同的看法。

sentences.en: That's a difference maker.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些认为这是一个错误的人，你能解释一下这个协议有什么值得做的吗？

sentences.en: But Senator, on the other hand, as you know, some of your Democratic colleagues, especially in the House, are saying that this is pretty weak tea, that you gave Republicans
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，这项协议将挽救生命。

sentences.en: too much power in this process and that you should not be agreeing to something this narrow
sentences.zh: 它不会结束这个国家的枪支暴力流行病。

sentences.en: because Republicans will just say they did something and will not come back to the issue, that this is it.
sentences.zh: 但我们为什么要放弃一个不仅能挽救一条生命，而是能挽救成千上万条生命的机会呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you obviously take a different view of that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这项法案虽然不是攻击性武器禁令。

sentences.en: But for those who think
sentences.zh: 我明白这一点。

sentences.en: is a mistake, can you explain what about this deal makes it worth doing?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这些对我们国家枪支法律的改变绝非装点门面。

sentences.en: Well, first and foremost, this deal is going to save lives.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，红旗法、打击枪支贩运者以及对21岁以下购买者进行新的背景调查将挽救大量生命。

sentences.en: It will not end the epidemic of gun violence in this nation.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们可以证明这不仅仅是渐进式的改变，

sentences.en: But why would we forego a possibility to save not one life, but thousands of lives?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们必须与共和党人找到共同点，但我们在一些确实会带来改变的变革上找到了共同点。

sentences.en: I mean, I think this bill is not an assault weapons ban.
sentences.zh: 但其次，我知道的是，这个国家没有任何伟大的社会变革运动在他们通过的第一项法案中就得到了他们想要的一切。

sentences.en: I get that.
sentences.zh: 看看婚姻平权运动。

sentences.en: But, you know, these are not window dressing changes to our nation's gun laws.
sentences.zh: 婚姻平权运动中发生的第一件事只是同性伴侣能够领养的简单权利。

sentences.en: There's no doubt that red flag statutes and crackdowns on gun traffickers and new background checks on purchasers under 21 will save tons of lives.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们本可以说，那不是同性婚姻。

sentences.en: So I think that we can make the case that this is not merely incremental change, that
sentences.zh: 我们不支持那个。

sentences.en: yes, we had to find common ground with Republicans, but we found common ground on a set of changes that actually will make a difference.
sentences.zh: 在我们得到一切之前，我们不支持任何事情。

sentences.en: But second, what I know is that no great social change movement in this country got everything they wanted in the first bill they passed.
sentences.zh: 但一旦那个变革通过，它就使其他变革成为可能。

sentences.en: Look at the marriage equality movement.
sentences.zh: 它突然让反对者相信，坐到谈判桌前并支持同性伴侣的更多权利是有政治利益的。

sentences.en: The first thing that happened in the marriage equality movement was just the simple right of gay couples to be able to adopt.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, folks could have said, that's not gay marriage.
sentences.zh: 所以鉴于这一切，在进入这些谈判时，你的策略是什么？

sentences.en: We're not supporting that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，明知之前许多次尝试都失败了，当然也包括2013年桑迪胡克小学枪击案后在枪支安全方面所做的努力。

sentences.en: We're not supporting anything until we get everything.
sentences.zh: 我认为我学到的教训是，第一，要现实地设定预期。

sentences.en: But once that change passed, it made other changes possible.
sentences.zh: 所以从一开始，我就公开表示，虽然我不会支持任何不能挽救生命的东西，但我只会支持有意义的方案。

sentences.en: It all of a sudden convinced opponents that there was political benefit to coming to the table and supporting more rights for gay couples.
sentences.zh: 我不会要求法案必须包含禁止攻击性武器之类的条款。

sentences.en: And it got us to the point eventually where we were able to pass marriage equality laws all around the country and get a constitutional change.
sentences.zh: 最终，我们得以在全国范围内通过婚姻平权法案，并实现了宪法层面的变革。

sentences.en: I just know that if you study great social change movements, making the first change, right, breaking the logjam is often what allows you, is almost universally what allows you
sentences.zh: 我深知，如果你研究过伟大的社会变革运动，就会发现实现最初的改变，打破僵局，几乎总是让你能够

sentences.en: to make all the other changes.
sentences.zh: 实现所有其他变革的关键。

sentences.en: And I think that this bill in and of itself is worth supporting.
sentences.zh: 我认为这项法案本身就值得支持。

sentences.en: If we never passed another bill, we should pass this bill because it will save lives.
sentences.zh: 即便我们此后再也无法通过其他法案，我们也应该通过这一项，因为它能挽救生命。

sentences.en: But that's not how this is going to work.
sentences.zh: 但事情并不会那样发展。

sentences.en: This will allow us to build bigger coalitions, to get more Republicans willing to support changes in the future.
sentences.zh: 这将使我们能够建立更广泛的联盟，让更多的共和党人愿意在未来支持变革。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So in some ways you see the gun safety movement like the marriage equality movement.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，你把枪支安全运动看作是婚姻平权运动的翻版。

sentences.en: I mean, can I guarantee that's going to happen here?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我能保证这种情况一定会发生吗？

sentences.en: No, that's why I argue, even if you don't believe that this is a pathway to future legislative success, you should still vote for it because it's going to make our country safer.
sentences.zh: 不能，这就是为什么我主张，即使你不相信这是未来立法成功的途径，你也应该投票支持它，因为它会让我们的国家更安全。

sentences.en: But I do think that this is the beginning, not the end.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这只是开始，而非终点。

sentences.en: I'm confident of that.
sentences.zh: 对此我深信不疑。

sentences.en: I mean, so given all of that, almost by definition, you're saying this has to be incremental to avoid scaring off Republicans, because this is about cultural change and it's slow.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，鉴于这一切，几乎可以肯定地说，你认为这必须是渐进式的，以避免吓跑共和党人，因为这关乎文化变革，而文化变革是缓慢的。

sentences.en: Well, I would also, you know, encourage folks that are saying we shouldn't pass this because it's
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也会鼓励那些说我们不应该通过这项法案的人，因为这

sentences.en: not enough to just go talk to parents out there, to just go talk to the folks I did last weekend in Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 还不够，去和家长们谈谈吧，去和上周末我在康涅狄格州见到的那些人谈谈。

sentences.en: I didn't meet anybody over the weekend who told me, don't pass anything until you get everything.
sentences.zh: 周末我没遇到任何人对我说，除非你拿到全部，否则什么都别通过。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a palpable anxiety out there in this country about the safety of our kids, about the safety of our public spaces.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这个国家，人们对于孩子们的安全、对于公共场所的安全，有着一种显而易见的焦虑。

sentences.en: And Americans want us to show progress.
sentences.zh: 美国人民希望我们展现出进步。

sentences.en: They want democracy to be able to sort of prove that it can respond at this moment.
sentences.zh: 他们希望民主制度能够证明它在当下是有所回应的。

sentences.en: So I get it that there are advocates and folks online who say, just keep the pressure on Republicans.
sentences.zh: 所以我明白，网上有一些倡导者和民众说，继续向共和党施压吧。

sentences.en: Don't agree to anything until you've broken them.
sentences.zh: 在彻底击垮他们之前，不要同意任何事。

sentences.en: I just don't think that that's how democracy should work.
sentences.zh: 我只是不认为民主应该这样运作。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that that's not what the people I represent want.
sentences.zh: 而且我敢肯定，这也不是我所代表的选民们想要的。

sentences.en: The people that I represent want us to make progress.
sentences.zh: 我所代表的选民希望我们取得进展。

sentences.en: Senator, do you think that these measures you all have agreed to would have stopped the Uvalde shooter or the Sandy Hook shooter?
sentences.zh: 参议员，你认为你们所有人达成的这些措施能阻止尤瓦尔迪或桑迪胡克的枪手吗？

sentences.en: I think there's a possibility that these changes could have made a difference in Uvalde.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些改变有可能在尤瓦尔迪事件中起到作用。

sentences.en: Of course, I can't be sure of that.
sentences.zh: 当然，我不能确定。

sentences.en: But if this bill leads to states passing red flag laws, a good red flag law could have made a difference in Texas.
sentences.zh: 但如果这项法案能促使各州通过“红旗法案”，那么一项好的红旗法案本可以在德克萨斯州发挥作用。

sentences.en: This young man showed all sorts of warning signs that could have triggered a red flag process.
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人表现出了各种各样的危险信号，本可以触发红旗程序。

sentences.en: You can never know for sure.
sentences.zh: 你永远无法确定。

sentences.en: But I think that, you know, we've designed a law that specifically with respect to Uvalde might have made the difference.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我们设计的这项法律，特别是在尤瓦尔迪事件方面，本可能带来不同的结果。

sentences.en: Senator, you're speaking to me from Connecticut, your home state, right?
sentences.zh: 参议员，你现在是从你的家乡康涅狄格州和我通话，对吧？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you've been there, I believe, since the deal was announced.
sentences.zh: 我相信自从协议宣布以来，你就一直待在那里。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you've talked to any of the Sandy Hook parents over the past couple of days.
sentences.zh: 我想知道过去几天你是否和桑迪胡克事件中受害者的家长们谈过。

sentences.en: I mean, I remember some of those parents were in the Senate gallery in 2013, when that package of gun safety laws failed.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我记得2013年那套枪支安全法案失败时，其中一些家长就在参议院旁听席上。

sentences.en: And some of them were very angry.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人当时非常愤怒。

sentences.en: What do they think about this deal?
sentences.zh: 他们对这次协议有什么看法？

sentences.en: What are they telling you?
sentences.zh: 他们对你说了什么？

sentences.en: Well, you know, the first thing to say is that there's no common opinion of anything amongst
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先要说的是，对于任何事情，这20位家长之间

sentences.en: 20 sets of parents.
sentences.zh: 并没有统一的意见。

sentences.en: But many of those parents are close friends.
sentences.zh: 但其中许多家长是亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: Many of the sons and daughters of the teachers who died that day are close friends.
sentences.zh: 那天遇难教师的许多子女也是亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: So of course, when we reached this deal late on
sentences.zh: 所以当然，当我们周六深夜达成这项协议时，

sentences.en: Saturday night, you know, some of my first calls and texts and emails were to those parents and sons and daughters.
sentences.zh: 我第一时间联系的一些人就是那些家长和他们的子女。

sentences.en: So I think I think they're frustrated that it took 10 years.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，他们对花了10年时间才达成协议感到沮丧。

sentences.en: I think they're continually heartbroken that it wasn't their tragedy that led to immediate change.
sentences.zh: 他们一直感到心碎，因为导致即时变革的不是他们当年的悲剧。

sentences.en: But to a person, they are incredibly grateful that this country is finally waking up to what's happening.
sentences.zh: 但他们每个人都无比感激这个国家终于开始意识到正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And I know that we didn't fix this problem.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们并没有解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And that if we pass this bill, we won't fix the epidemic of mass shootings, but that the log jam is breaking, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我们通过这项法案，我们无法根除大规模枪击事件的流行，但僵局正在打破，对吧？

sentences.en: The 30 years of inaction is ending.
sentences.zh: 30年的不作为正在终结。

sentences.en: I just, you know, I wish this happened 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我只是希望这一切能早10年发生。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我确实这么想。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry that it wasn't the shooting in Sandy Hook that inspired my colleagues to change.
sentences.zh: 我很遗憾，桑迪胡克枪击案没能激励我的同事们做出改变。

sentences.en: But I've learned in the last 10 years that that's not how politics works.
sentences.zh: 但在过去的10年里，我学到政治并不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: There's very few epiphanies.
sentences.zh: 顿悟时刻非常少见。

sentences.en: There's very few 180 degree turns that a big place like Washington makes.
sentences.zh: 像华盛顿这样庞大的机构，很少会发生180度的大转弯。

sentences.en: It often is a slog over years, sometimes decades to make change happen.
sentences.zh: 变革往往需要数年，有时甚至是数十年的艰苦努力才能实现。

sentences.en: And this to me is a seminal moment where that turn is happening.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一个具有开创性的时刻，转折正在发生。

sentences.en: And my belief over the weekend talking to a lot of the families in Connecticut is that that really matters to them.
sentences.zh: 周末与康涅狄格州的许多家庭交谈后，我相信这对他们来说意义重大。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And Senator, what happens if this fails?
sentences.zh: 参议员，如果这次失败了会怎样？

sentences.en: What you have in hand is an agreement on a framework, right?
sentences.zh: 你手中掌握的是一份框架协议，对吧？

sentences.en: And 10 Republican senators have signed on to it.
sentences.zh: 而且有10位共和党参议员已经签署了。

sentences.en: But there's a long history, of course, of framework deals falling apart as they turn into actual language of a law.
sentences.zh: 但当然，框架协议在转化为实际法律条文的过程中分崩离析的先例有很多。

sentences.en: If this too goes down, what will you do?
sentences.zh: 如果这次也失败了，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: You know, two weeks ago, when these negotiations began, I was preparing for failure.
sentences.zh: 你知道，两周前谈判开始时，我已经在为失败做准备了。

sentences.en: I was emotionally and psychologically preparing myself and, you know, the families for failure.
sentences.zh: 我在情感和心理上都在为自己，以及那些家庭，做着失败的准备。

sentences.en: I'm not preparing for failure anymore.
sentences.zh: 但我现在不再为失败做准备了。

sentences.en: I believe that we are going to pass this bill.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们一定会通过这项法案。

sentences.en: And I believe that because we've never come this far.
sentences.zh: 我相信这一点，因为我们从未走得这么远。

sentences.en: We've never had this big a coalition.
sentences.zh: 我们从未拥有过如此庞大的联盟。

sentences.en: We've never had a movement as strong as we do today.
sentences.zh: 我们从未拥有过像今天这样强大的运动。

sentences.en: I am no longer preparing for failure as I have every single time I've entered into negotiations like this over the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我不再像过去10年里每次参与此类谈判时那样为失败做准备了。

sentences.en: I am now preparing to pass this bill.
sentences.zh: 我现在正准备通过这项法案。

sentences.en: So maybe I'm unrealistic.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我不切实际。

sentences.en: Maybe I should understand how difficult this is.
sentences.zh: 也许我应该明白这有多困难。

sentences.en: But I've
sentences.zh: 但我已经

sentences.en: I've crossed the Rubicon.
sentences.zh: 我已经破釜沉舟了。

sentences.en: We're getting this done.
sentences.zh: 我们一定会完成这件事。

sentences.en: And what does that feel like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, this was an issue that was thrust upon you, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种程度上说，这是一个强加给你的议题，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Sandy Hook happened right after you were elected U.S.
sentences.zh: 桑迪胡克事件发生在你当选美国参议员之后不久。

sentences.en: Senator.
sentences.zh: 参议员。

sentences.en: And Sandy Hook was your constituency as U.S.
sentences.zh: 而桑迪胡克曾是你担任美国众议员时的选区。

sentences.en: Congressman.
sentences.zh: 国会议员。

sentences.en: It's this issue that sort of found you.
sentences.zh: 是这个议题找到了你。

sentences.en: But it's brought you so much failure.
sentences.zh: 但它也带给你如此多的挫败。

sentences.en: So how are you feeling right now?
sentences.zh: 所以你现在感觉如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, but I mean, my my failure on this issue is inconsequential compared to the loss of the families and the failure of the system to stand up for them and their kids safety.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我的意思是，我在这个问题上的失败，与那些家庭的损失以及体制未能保护他们和孩子安全相比，微不足道。

sentences.en: So I just wake up every day feeling so lucky that my kids are with me in this fight.
sentences.zh: 所以我每天醒来都感到非常幸运，因为我的孩子们和我站在一起参与这场斗争。

sentences.en: I hope this bill passes, but there's still so much more to do.
sentences.zh: 我希望这项法案能通过，但还有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: You know, my life was changed by what happened in Sandy Hook.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的生活因桑迪胡克事件而改变。

sentences.en: But even if this bill passes, it doesn't stop the fact that I'm going to just continue to order my life in a way that presses for more change.
sentences.zh: 但即使这项法案通过了，我也不会停止以推动更多变革的方式来安排我的生活。

sentences.en: The package would still need to pass the House.

sentences.en: On Monday, lawmakers in Washington held the second day of hearings investigating the causes of the January 6th attack on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周一，华盛顿的议员们举行了调查1月6日美国国会大厦袭击事件起因的第二天听证会。

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 国会大厦。

sentences.en: A committee of lawmakers played video testimony from some of Donald Trump's closest associates, including former Attorney General William Barr.
sentences.zh: 一个议员委员会播放了唐纳德·特朗普最亲密的几位助手，包括前司法部长威廉·巴尔的视频证词。

sentences.en: The associates said they objected when Mr. Trump claimed he was the rightful winner of the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 这些助手表示，当特朗普先生声称自己是2020年大选的合法获胜者时，他们表示了反对。

sentences.en: I was somewhat demoralized because I thought, boy, if he really believes this stuff, he has, you know, he's become detached from reality.
sentences.zh: 我当时有些沮丧，因为我想，天哪，如果他真的相信这些东西，那他已经脱离现实了。

sentences.en: Mr. Barr said in his testimony that when he told Trump, quote, how crazy some of these allegations were, he said Trump did not seem interested in what was actually true.
sentences.zh: 巴尔先生在证词中说，当他告诉特朗普，引用他的话，“这些指控有多么疯狂”时，他说特朗普似乎对什么是事实并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: There was never an indication of interest in what the actual facts were.
sentences.zh: 他从未表现出对实际事实的兴趣。

sentences.en: Committee members said Trump used claims of election fraud to get his supporters to donate to a fund that they believed would help overturn the results.
sentences.zh: 委员会成员表示，特朗普利用选举舞弊的说法，诱导支持者向一个他们认为有助于推翻选举结果的基金捐款。

sentences.en: Throughout the committee's investigation, we found evidence that the Trump campaign and its surrogates
sentences.zh: 在整个委员会的调查过程中，我们发现证据表明特朗普竞选团队及其代理人

sentences.en: misled donors as to where their funds would go and what they would be used for.
sentences.zh: 误导了捐赠者，让他们以为资金会流向何处以及会被用于何处。

sentences.en: But a committee investigator said there was no evidence that the $100 million that supporters donated was ever used for that purpose.
sentences.zh: 但一位委员会调查员表示，没有证据表明支持者捐赠的1亿美元被用于该目的。

sentences.en: So not only was there the big lie, there was the big ripoff.
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅有“弥天大谎”，还有“弥天大骗局”。
